summary: Separating provider trust from model capability closes a real governance gap: the same model can have materially different retention, access, contractual and operational properties depending on where it runs.

points.text: NIST's AI and supply-chain frameworks both treat third-party risk as a lifecycle concern, supporting provider review that is independent of benchmark quality or model identity.
A matrix becomes operational only when its cells map to dispatch decisions over data class, capability and environment; a prose vendor assessment alone cannot prevent a disallowed route.
Evidence should include contractual retention, training use, residency, subprocessors, identity controls, incident response and service configuration because provider trust is multidimensional.
Every entry needs evidence provenance, expiry and a re-evaluation trigger; certifications and terms can change while the model name remains constant.
